headline: High risk of prompt injection and cascading errors: Cline can read/write workspace files and use MCP, while Plane exposes file uploads and external API surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline can read/write workspace files and use MCP, so it may ingest attacker-controlled content from shared files or servers. Plane exposes file uploads and hyperlinks/notes, which can carry malicious instructions if Cline processes them as trusted input. The pairwise bridge is plausible in default workspace-based workflows, though not directly documented.
conditions: IF Plane content is copied into a shared workspace file that Cline reads
IF Cline is connected to an MCP server that relays Plane content without provenance tags
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of shared files into Cline prompts
Require provenance labels on any Plane-derived content before Cline reads it
Restrict MCP servers to trusted, read-only sources
Use separate workspaces for Plane exports and Cline tasks

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cline touches source code and browser screenshots and has broad network egress; Plane stores issues, tasks, roadmaps, files, images, and notes. If both are pointed at the same workspace or upload path, sensitive project data can flow from Plane into Cline outputs or external model calls. The profiles show a plausible shared-file leakage path, but not a guaranteed one.
conditions: IF Plane uploads are placed in the same workspace directory Cline reads
IF Cline sends workspace contents to its model provider during analysis
mitigations: Keep Plane uploads outside Cline's workspace
Redact secrets from files before Cline opens them
Turn off unnecessary file attachments in Plane workflows
Use a separate account or workspace for sensitive artifacts

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cline can write the filesystem and modify git state, while Plane is not writable locally but can still receive uploaded files and API-driven updates. The main conflict is on shared mutable resources: Cline may change repo state while Plane tracks related tasks or files, creating coordination errors even though Plane itself lacks local write capability. Uncertainty about the exact integration pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Plane task artifacts are mirrored into the same git workspace Cline edits
IF multiple Cline instances operate on the same repository without locking
mitigations: Assign one writer per repository branch
Use git locks or branch-per-task conventions
Keep Plane attachments read-only in the coding workspace
Run Cline and Plane in separate directories

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can generate code, browser-derived findings, and file edits that Plane may then store as issues, tasks, or notes. Plane's workflow surfaces suggest it can preserve and redistribute those outputs, so an error in Cline can cascade into planning or scheduling artifacts if Plane treats them as authoritative. The interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Plane imports Cline-generated text into issues or notes without review
IF downstream users act on Plane entries that originated from Cline outputs
mitigations: Require human review before Plane accepts Cline-generated artifacts
Mark Cline outputs as unverified in Plane
Separate exploratory findings from actionable tasks
Add a verification checklist before scheduling or assignment

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and do not declare conflicting residency or regulated-data handling, so no direct compliance breach is evidenced. However, Plane handles files and notes while Cline handles browser screenshots and model-provider API keys, so a compliance gap could arise if regulated data is placed into either system. The other agent is not separately cited because no specific cross-border or certification mismatch is documented.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is entered into Plane or Cline
IF the deployed model provider or Plane hosting region lacks the required controls
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in either tool
Confirm hosting region and retention settings before use
Document a data-class policy for uploads and screenshots
Use separate environments for regulated and non-regulated work
